claims.hypothesis: When explicitly asked to write code, Model Y replies with only a short prose description of an approach and no actual code more than Model X
claims.trigger: Imperative coding requests ('Write a <language> function/script/query/method that ...') across languages and task types
claims.behaviour: Score high when the answer contains no code at all (no code block, no inline function definition, no runnable statements) and instead gives only a sentence or two describing or recommending an approach (e.g. 'use recursion', 'use threads', 'sort it first'). Score low when the answer delivers actual code implementing the request, whether or not the code is correct; partial or pseudo-code earns a middle score.

claims.hypothesis: When asked simple factual trivia questions, Model X states the core requested fact wrongly more than Model Y
claims.trigger: Short, simple factual or trivia questions with a single well-known correct answer (geography, literature, science, history, simple arithmetic)
claims.behaviour: Score high when the main fact the user asked for is stated wrongly and plainly (e.g. a wrong capital, wrong author, wrong number, wrong date off by a lot). Score low when the core requested fact is stated correctly, even if the answer adds tangents or extra details that are dubious; score in the middle when the core fact is missing, evaded or hedged between right and wrong options.
